name: Salmon Patties with Potatoes and Green Beans

components.name: Salmon Patties
steps: Pan-cook 650 g salmon in 10 ml oil to 63 C, cool briefly and flake carefully, removing any remaining skin or bones.
In the same pan soften diced onion and red pepper with minced garlic, then cool slightly.
Mix salmon, aromatics, almond flour, 100 g beaten egg, 25 g mayonnaise, mustard, parsley, dill, salt and pepper. Shape into eight equal patties.
Heat 25 ml oil in a heavy skillet and cook patties in batches, turning gently until browned and hot throughout.

components.name: Potatoes & Green Beans
steps: Boil potatoes in a saucepan until tender; cook green beans separately or steam over the potato pot. Toss with butter and the remaining salt.

components.name: Lemon-Dill Dressing
steps: Mix yogurt, 35 g mayonnaise, lemon juice and dill into a cold dressing. Serve two patties per person with potatoes and beans, keeping dressing separate.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.

Original Downshiftology patties use roasted salmon, almond flour, egg, mayo and mustard, and may be cooked on stovetop. UNHANGRY uses pan-cooked salmon, adds potatoes/beans and reduces dressing quantity to make four substantial meals.
Storing & reheating: Freeze cooked salmon patties and potatoes separately; green beans soften after thawing. Mayonnaise dressing is refrigerated only.
Freezer: patties and plain potatoes; keep dressing apart
Allergens: Fish, Dairy, Egg, Tree nuts

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish to 63°C, shrimp and shellfish until opaque and firm (mussels must open), and reheat to at least 74°C.

flags.shelfLife: Salmon patties — plan for days 1-3; freeze later-week portions. Dressing is fridge-only.

foodSafety: Refrigerate perishables promptly in shallow containers: within 2 hours after cooking, or within 1 hour if the air temperature is above 32 C.
Store at 4 C or colder. General cooked-leftover limit: 3-4 days; for delicate seafood recipes follow any shorter specific limit above.
Freeze later-week portions promptly, if this recipe is flagged freezer-suitable; thaw in refrigerator, not on a kitchen counter.
For fish, target a safe cooked internal temperature of 63 C; shrimp and shellfish should be cooked until opaque / firm, and mussels must open during cooking.
Reheat leftovers thoroughly to 74 C, avoiding repeated reheating and cooling cycles.
Cooked rice requires rapid chilling, appropriate cold storage and thorough reheating. Rice left warm for a prolonged period is not made safe by reheating.
Shellfish, fish, soy, dairy, wheat, egg, nuts and pork vary by recipe; verify allergens and dietary restrictions before importing.
